tox_values.unit: ug/kg bw/day, expressed as DEHP equivalents
tox_values.basis: Reduction in fetal testosterone (common mode of action); DEHP as index compound; DINP included conservatively. Temporary (t-TDI) per Reg. 2023/1442 recitals 6-7. DIDP not in group. Apply as: sum_i(intake_i x RPF_i) <= 50 ug/kg bw/day.

tox_values.unit: ug/kg bw/day (individual t-TDI, not in group)

tox_values.basis: RPF = TDI_DEHP / HBGV_i (COT summary of EFSA method). DBP 5, BBP 0.1, DEHP 1 VERIFIED via the DEHP-eq formula in Reg. 2023/1442 entry 36 and consistent with TDI ratios. DIBP 4 VERIFIED (Commission, entry 36; DIBP not in EFSA group). DINP 0.3 = UNVERIFIED: the EFSA table was not accessible; COT states an extra factor 3.3 was applied for DINP; 0.05/0.15 = 0.33. DINP is excluded from the regulatory DEHP-eq sum.
Th17 cell increase in mice (immune); reference point 8.2 ng/kg bw/day HED; overall UF 50. Replaces 2015 t-TDI of 4 ug/kg bw/day.
Increased relative liver weight; LOAEL 19 mg/kg-day; UF 1000; medium confidence. Also oral slope factor 1.4e-2 per mg/kg-day (B2, 1988).
90-day rat drinking-water study (potassium antimony tartrate), NOAEL 6.0 mg/kg bw/day (body weight gain, food/water intake), UF 1000. Drinking-water GV 20 ug/L.

DERIVED: NOAEL 7.7 mg/kg bw/day (2-yr rat drinking-water study, Beliles 1985) / UF 1000 (10x10x10 incl. carcinogenicity/genotoxicity); WHO GV 0.02 mg/L at 60 kg. TDI value itself not read on a WHO page: treat as UNVERIFIED-derived. Year of WHO assessment not confirmed.
tox_values.source: Australian Drinking Water Guidelines styrene page citing WHO, https://guidelines.nhmrc.gov.au/australian-drinking-water-guidelines/part-5/physical-chemical-characteristics/styrene-vinylbenzene

tox_values.basis: 2020 opinion (IARC Monograph 121 impact): no evidence styrene from FCM raises cancer risk, but genotoxicity data gaps. 2025 opinion (EFSA Journal pub 9473): no evidence of oral mutagenicity; no health concern if migration does not exceed the Commission-proposed 40 ug/kg food. No numeric HBGV found.

fccmigex_summary: FCCmigex (Food Packaging Forum; Geueke et al. 2022, Crit Rev Food Sci Nutr, doi:10.1080/10408398.2022.2067828) systematically maps 1,210 studies and 22,522 entries; 2,881 of 3,142 food contact chemicals investigated were detected. Plastics are the most studied material (759 studies, 1,975 chemicals detected; >1,000 detected migrating into food/simulants, mostly from single-use items). Entries by polymer: PE 1,842, PP 1,763, multilayer 1,306, PET 1,258 (rPET 207), PS 880, PA 753, PVC 736. Across plastics DEHP and DBP are the two most commonly found chemicals; DiBP, DEHA, BHT, the antioxidant breakdown product 2,4-di-tert-butylphenol and cyclic siloxanes D5/D6 are also among the most frequent; BPA mainly from polycarbonate. The paper does not give per-polymer rankings (the online dashboard allows filtering by 12 polymers), and it does not specifically discuss Sb in PET or styrene in PS. Sources: https://bura.brunel.ac.uk/bitstream/2438/25123/1/FullText.pdf ; https://foodpackagingforum.org/news/fccmigex-dashboard-now-has-in-depth-plastics-page
notes: Phthalates are PVC plasticisers. For PP the only quantitative content data found are two Chinese studies (DBP/DIBP/DEHP up to ~1-3 mg/kg, often ND). No content data were found for CPET trays, PET-coated board or lidding films. Do not invent defaults for DINP in PP/PET.

Under Reg 2023/1442 DBP and DEHP may be used as plasticisers only in repeated-use articles for non-fatty food, so their presence in single-use PP/PET packaging is as a contaminant (or technical support agent at <=0.05-0.1%), not an intended additive.

Microwave phthalate data suitable for validation are thin: Moreira et al. 2014 (PP, water, 210-700 W, 1-30 min) gives DBP <LOQ-2.0 ug/L new and <LOQ-7.5 ug/L for 1-year-used containers; BBP ND. Per-condition values are only in figures.

Haldimann et al. 2013 is the best CPET validation set but is conventional oven 200 C/30 min. The same paper (citing Haldimann et al. 2007, Food Addit Contam 24:860-868) states microwave heating gives lower Sb migration than conventional oven heating, and that some ready meals in the 2007 study exceeded 40 ug/kg. The 2007 numbers were not accessible (PubMed page did not load).

Haldimann 2013 diffusion parameters (D0 = 3.6e14 cm2/s, Ea = 188 kJ/mol, 62% diffusible Sb) can parametrise an Arrhenius/Fickian Sb model for CPET. Note that 'Haldimann 2013' is about one CPET lasagne tray type and filled-to-brim trays overstate typical retail conditions.
Welle & Franz 2011 (Sb in PET bottles, activation-energy model) was identified but its numeric values were not retrieved; cited only through the 2023 Molecules review.

Microwave degrades PP antioxidants in fatty/ethanolic simulants (Alin & Hakkarainen, KTH) and Irgafos 168 in PP (11.7% degradation, Yang et al. 2016), producing 2,4-DTBP and oxidised Irgafos 168 (NIAS).

Chang et al. 2019 (J Food Eng 244:142-149, doi:10.1016/j.jfoodeng.2018.09.028) modelled BHT and Irganox 1010 migration from PP including 700 W microwave; model overestimated HPLC values by 1.5-2x; no numbers in abstract (https://scholar.korea.ac.kr/handle/2021.sw.korea/67163?mode=full).
Liu et al. 2020: PP lunch-box DBP/DIBP mobility into isooctane ~9-10% at 4-40 C, rising quickly at 60 C (first-order k1 0.2256 for DBP at 60 C, units not stated).

Recommended app defaults (compiler suggestion): adult 70 kg (EFSA 2012) with a toggle for 60 kg (the convention behind SMLs and WHO GVs); child 12 kg toddler; infant 5 kg. For phthalate group risk, compute DEHP-eq = 1*DEHP + 5*DBP + 0.1*BBP (+4*DIBP if modelled) and compare with 50 ug/kg bw/day; handle DINP against its own 150 ug/kg bw/day TDI unless the user opts to add it at RPF 0.3 (UNVERIFIED).

UNVERIFIED items: DINP RPF 0.3; unit of Lan et al. 2022 PP phthalate contents; typical Irgafos 168 loading (500-2000 mg/kg); residual styrene in PS; WHO styrene TDI 7.7 ug/kg bw/day (derived from NOAEL/UF, not read on WHO page); styrene SML 0.04 mg/kg adoption status; Hussain 2023 microwave power 1000 W (press report only); 250 mg/kg central Sb default; Sb in PET-coated board.

Not checked in this session: Regulation (EU) 2024/3190 restricting BPA in food contact materials; EFSA 2026 draft update of default values (COT paper TOX-2026-13 exists: https://cot.food.gov.uk/sites/default/files/2026-03/TOX-2026-13%20EFSA%20consultation%20on%20UF%20and%20DVs%20Acc%20V%20SO.pdf), which may change the 70/12/5 kg defaults.
